deployment.mechanism: Inno Setup installer (OllamaSetup.exe), per-user install — not an MSI.
deployment.mechanism_evidence: Verified 2026-09-09, read-only, live host: (1) `Get-Command ollama` resolves to `C:\Users\Matt Becker\AppData\Local\Programs\Ollama\ollama.exe` — a per-user AppData path, not Program Files; (2) registry Uninstall entry found under HKCU (not HKLM) at `SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{44E83376-CE68-45EB-8FC1-393500EB558C}_is1` — the `_is1` suffix and `UninstallString` pointing at `unins000.exe` are Inno Setup's standard signature, and no `WindowsInstaller` property is present (an MSI-backed entry always carries `WindowsInstaller=1`), so this is confirmed not an MSI and Node's ProductCode/UpgradeCode check does not apply. DisplayName 'Ollama version 0.32.6', Publisher 'Ollama'.
deployment.models_path_evidence: `$env:OLLAMA_MODELS` is unset at User/Machine/Process scope — per CLAUDE.md's absent-env-var rule, this was NOT read as confirming the documented default. Instead confirmed from Ollama's own reported effective config: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server-1.log`, repeated 'server config' log lines (e.g. timestamp 2026-08-28T13:34:47), carry `OLLAMA_MODELS:C:\\Users\\Matt Becker\\.ollama\\models` — this happens to match the documented default but is recorded here as Ollama's own statement of it, not an assumption.
deployment.ollama_host_evidence: Same server-config log lines carry `OLLAMA_HOST:http://127.0.0.1:11434` — matches CLAUDE.md's 'Ollama runs natively at 127.0.0.1:11434'.
deployment.caddy_model_evidence: Confirmed live, not from notes — the pinball caddy's `C:\automation\caddy\scripts\caddy-server.js` line 354 hardcodes `const MODEL = 'qwen3.5-caddy';`, called via POST to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat` (never `/api/generate` — the file's own comment says the latter ignores `think:false` for the qwen3.5 series) with `think:false` and `keep_alive:-1` as top-level fields. `ollama list` on the live host shows `qwen3.5-caddy:latest` present (10 GB, pulled/derived 6 weeks ago) alongside the unrelated base tags `qwen3.5:9b-q8_0` and `gemma4:latest`. This supersedes any note referencing `qwen3:14b` (stale) or the base `qwen3.5:9b-q8_0` tag (not what the caddy actually calls) — neither is the caddy model.

open-webui.evidence: Confirmed live via `docker inspect open-webui --format '{{json .Config.Env}}'` (2026-09-09): env includes `OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434`.

openclaw.evidence: `docker inspect openclaw`'s env list carries no `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` or equivalent — openclaw's Ollama connectivity is apparently set via its own provider config file inside its data volume (`openclaw_data` → `/home/node/.openclaw`), not a container env var. Per CLAUDE.md's hard boundary ('OpenClaw config — read version only, never edit'), that config file was not inspected. The only documented value is in the planning doc `C:\automation\caddy\openclaw-environment-spec-v1.md` §4.1: `baseUrl: "http://host.docker.internal:11434"` (native `api: "ollama"`, no `/v1` suffix) — a spec, not a live-confirmed fact. Note: this same `docker inspect` call surfaced openclaw's live secrets (Telegram bot token, gateway password) in tool output; they were not recorded anywhere on disk and this project does not otherwise touch openclaw config.

downgrade_safety_research.range_checked: docker-v29.6.1 -> docker-v29.8.0 (target), individually against GitHub release notes for docker-v29.6.2, docker-v29.7.0, docker-v29.7.1, docker-v29.7.2, docker-v29.8.0 — not just a summarized docs page.
downgrade_safety_research.finding: No storage-format, data-layout, graphdriver, or containerd-snapshotter change is named in any of the five release notes across this range. The only functionally relevant change found is 29.7.0 starting to honor `max-concurrent-downloads`/`max-concurrent-uploads` (daemon.json, unrelated to storage format).
downgrade_safety_research.caveat: This is 'no breaking change publicly named across the full range', not a Docker-issued downgrade certification — Docker does not publish explicit downgrade guarantees for the engine. Recorded as evidence for Matt's Phase 4 decision if a rollback is ever needed, not as a guarantee.

deployment.mechanism: manual MSI installer (official nodejs.org Windows x64 .msi, run by hand — not nvm-windows, not winget-installed)
deployment.mechanism_evidence: Verified 2026-09-08, read-only, live host: (1) no nvm — no `nvm` command, no NVM_HOME/NVM_SYMLINK env vars, no nvm install directories; (2) `C:\Program Files\nodejs` is a real directory, not a symlink/junction (nvm-windows would symlink this path); (3) registry Uninstall entry has WindowsInstaller=1, ProductCode {6178C0C7-8EA8-458F-8060-E49E500A666F}, InstallSource 'C:\Users\Matt Becker\Downloads\'; (4) the exact installer file (node-v24.18.0-x64.msi, retained in Downloads, dated 2026-07-07) carries that same ProductCode in its own Property table, read via the WindowsInstaller COM API in read-only mode. `winget list --id OpenJS.NodeJS` does match this install for upgrade-tracking, but that reflects winget's ARP-matching against its package database, not the install method — InstallSource is Matt's own Downloads folder, not winget's cache.
deployment.update_behavior: In-place replace, not a side-install. The installed MSI has a populated UpgradeCode — the Windows Installer field that drives the standard major-upgrade sequence (RemoveExistingProducts against any prior ProductCode sharing that UpgradeCode) when a newer MSI is run. Confirmed read-only against the retained 24.18.0 installer's own Property table via the WindowsInstaller COM `OpenDatabase` API (opens the file, installs nothing), then re-confirmed 2026-09-08 against the downloaded v24.20.0 target MSI before Matt applied it — both carry UpgradeCode {47C07A3A-42EF-4213-A85D-8F5A59077C28}. The real update ran 2026-09-08 (run `20260908-220239`): registry confirms the live install now carries ProductCode {DC5BBE4F-0668-40DC-A913-83710DA79E35}, DisplayVersion 24.20.0, InstallSource still Matt's own Downloads folder — in-place replace behaved exactly as predicted.
